description: **October 24, 1929**, Wall Street collapses. In three years, unemployment has affected **25%** of Americans and the crisis opens the way to extremes in Europe.

hero.hook: A Thursday on Wall Street, and the world falls into a decade of misery.

blocks.text: **October 24, 1929**, **Black Thursday**, the New York Stock Exchange collapses. It's not just a financial accident. It is the beginning of the **Great Depression**, a global economic paralysis.

In three years, the wealth produced in the world falls by approximately **15%**. Unemployment affects **25%** of Americans. European democracies are faltering. This is how a bubble took everything away.

In the **Roaring Twenties** (the 1920s), America consumed on credit: cars, radios, household appliances. Between 1920 and 1929, the **Dow Jones**, the index that measures the price of major American stocks, multiplied by six. The engine of the bubble: the . We borrow to buy securities, betting on their rise. [[Buying stocks on margin]]

blocks.caption: The Roaring Twenties: euphoria, credit and speculation.

blocks.text: On the day of the crash, on the Chicago Stock Exchange, brokers allegedly hung a virtual stork... accused of having brought misfortune instead of prosperity.

From 1928, production stagnated and agricultural prices fell. Factories make more than people can buy: it's . The market is , too expensive compared to reality. When doubt prevails, everyone sells at the same time. [[overproduction]] [[overvalued]]

sections.title: The Roaring Twenties and the bubble

blocks.text: On **October 24**, eleven million sell orders. On **29**, “Black Tuesday”, the fall accelerates. Between 1929 and 1932, the market lost **89%** of its value. Then come the : waves of customers who withdraw their money in panic. About **9,000** US banks are going bankrupt. [[bank runs]]

blocks.caption: Queues of the unemployed: the social face of the crisis.

blocks.text: Broke Americans hitched horses to their cars to save gas. They were called the “Hoover Cars”, after the name of President , considered too passive in the face of the crisis. [[Herbert Hoover]]
Without credit, factories close. Production drops by approximately **46%**. Without social protection worthy of the name, millions of people depend on soup kitchens.

sections.title: From the crash to the bankruptcy of banks

blocks.text: The United States repatriates its loans. Europe is asphyxiating. The , a system where currencies are linked to gold, propagates the crisis: to keep gold, central banks raise interest rates, which further slows down the economy. [[Gold Standard]]

policies (lowering prices and wages to “clean up”) are failing. In Germany, unemployment reaches **30%**. Adolf Hitler exploits desperation against , the fragile German republic. In **January 1933**, he came to power. The economic crisis opens the door to political catastrophe. [[deflation]] [[Weimar]]

Elected in **1932**, **Franklin D. Roosevelt** launches the . End of pure , the idea that the State should not touch the market. The State is banking on the : major works, regulation of banks, start of social protection. The recovery remained fragile... until the mobilization of 1941. [[Roosevelt's New Deal (1933)]] [[laissez-faire]] [[RELAUNCH]]
After the crash of **1929**, the Dow Jones lost **89%** of its value, **25%** of Americans were unemployed, and the crisis favored the arrival of Hitler to power in **1933**.
